extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants (especially those triaged / 'not discussed') preparing a resubmission or new submission
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, emotional, and strategic preparation for resubmitting an NIH grant application (A1), submitting a new application (A0), or pivoting to a different mechanism or agency after an application was triaged/not discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decipher your Summary Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Start your resubmission work by figuring out how to decipher your Summary Statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author emphasizes that preparation 'starts with figuring out how to decipher your Summary Statement.' Use the Summary Statement to identify reviewer concerns and to guide which changes are needed before resubmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond to more than just 'Approach' critiques
rubrics_metrics.description: A successful resubmission requires addressing more than only the critiques of your Approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The post warns: 'There’s more to a successful resubmission than responding to the critiques about your Approach. (A lot more.)' This implies reviewers may have concerns across multiple application sections (significance, investigators, innovation, environment, etc.) and you should comprehensively address all relevant critique areas rather than focusing narrowly on methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow time to process emotions before revising
rubrics_metrics.description: Give yourself time to process disappointment and emotions after receiving a triage/not discussed outcome before starting revision work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The post opens with empathetic advice: 'Once you’ve had some time to process your feelings about it (and you definitely should), it’s time to dust yourself off and figure out what’s next.' This is presented as an explicit step before beginning resubmission planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose the appropriate next submission strategy (A1, A0, or pivot)
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide whether to submit an amended resubmission (A1), a new submission (A0), or pivot to a different funding mechanism or agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author notes the resubmission guidance applies whether that’s 'an actual resubmission (A1), a new submission (A0), or a pivot to a different funding mechanism or agency.' Consider strategic trade-offs among these options when planning revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use targeted training/resources to structure your resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek structured training or resources that outline the concrete moves required for a successful resubmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The post promotes a ~30 minute training that 'walks you through the five moves you need to make for a successful NIH resubmission.' It recommends using such a resource (available in the author's free resource library) to get a stepwise plan rather than improvising.
